correctness.rationale: A continuous equivariant injection is a finite-radius block code and maps the two fixed configurations injectively onto the two fixed configurations. If it swaps them, two far-separated length-\(m\) zero blocks amidst ones yield two disjoint finite output-one islands; all sufficiently large separating lengths would have to be multiples of \(n\), impossible. If it preserves them, two single-one defects separated by \(km\) zero symbols yield an output inter-island gap \(km+a-b\) for each large \(k\), so \(n\) divides \(m\). If \(n\) divides \(m\), inclusion is an embedding. The right-resolving \(j\)-state graph has finite-to-one labeling and Perron equation \(\lambda^j=\lambda^{j-1}+1\), giving the strict entropy comparison. All quantifiers and boundaries \(m,n\ge2\) are covered.

value.rationale: This exact infinite family classification resolves a naturally parameterized sofic-shift embedding question, not an arbitrary isolated numerical slice. It exhibits infinitely many pairs satisfying strict entropy order but failing to embed, and gives a simple algebraic decision procedure for every pair, clarifying the difference between entropy/period tests and finite-island asymptotics. The finite-radius two-defect mechanism is structural.
